subject: FinPay evaluation — TCO & next tests (Redwood vs hyperscalers)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finpay.com>, Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay — follow-up & proposed next tests (TCO + perf)

Hi Samantha / Arjun —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Recap:
- Key use case: realtime fraud detection enrichment (~1.5k requests/sec peak, avg payload ~600 tokens/request if we include context).
- Primary eval criteria: p95 latency < 120ms for the single-request path, unit cost per 1M tokens, and consistent output quality compared to your current Anthropic setup.
- Current deployment constraints: must pass procurement/security checklist; SOC2 audit evidence is required for pilot.

What we propose next (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood to deliver a TCO sketch and micro-benchmark (attached spreadsheet + summary PDF).
2) Redwood runs a 1M-token synthetic workload with your representative prompt set and returns: effective cost per 1M tokens, cache hit assumptions, batching uplift, and p95/p50 latency numbers.
3) FinPay runs the same synthetic suite against your Anthropic/hyperscaler baseline (we can share the harness).
4) Compare results and tune: batching settings, KV/prefix cache, and model variants.

Assumptions we used in the attached TCO sheet (high-level):
- Request profile: 600 tokens/request average payload, 12 tokens generated avg.
- Baseline batch window: 10ms (continuous batching) -> typical batching uplift 1.6x for 512 seq workloads.
- Cache: assuming 30% prefix reuse for this workload (we can tune).

Immediate asks from your side:
- Confirm the representative prompt set you want us to use (or we can use the subset you shared in the doc).
- Confirm a 2-hour benchmarking window next week where we can run load against your test endpoint and the Redwood hosted endpoint.

Attached: redwood-tco-modeling.xlsx (inputs + scenarios), redwood-benchmarks-summary.pdf (sample results & methodology).

If this looks good I’ll book time for the run and loop in Marcus for dedicated/Dedicated-capacity questions.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear next steps and the attachments. Quick responses/questions before we schedule the run: 

1) Cost assumptions: can you provide a simple per-1M-tokens table (Redwood hosted, Redwood dedicated amortized per-1M, Anthropic baseline, AWS Bedrock baseline) with the assumptions used (tokens counted, generation vs prompt split, cache hit %)? Procurement will want this at a glance.

2) Cache hit baseline: we typically see ~20–25% prefix reuse today for our fraud rules. If you assume 30% in your spreadsheet, can you also show the sensitivity at 10%, 25%, and 40%?

3) Batching: we’re worried about p95 with bursty traffic — please include an assumed burst profile (1s spikes to 1.5k RPS) and how continuous batching behaves.

4) Security artifacts: procurement asked for SOC2 type II and a brief on network isolation options for Dedicated. Marcus — can you confirm what artifacts Redwood can provide for a pilot?

We can do the 2-hour window on Tue Aug 17 10–12 PDT if that works. Please share the harness or we can run ours if you prefer.

Samantha

Subject: Re: FinPay — follow-up & proposed next tests (TCO + perf)

Thanks Samantha — notes inline and the quick table below. I’ve also updated the attached spreadsheet to include the sensitivity bands you asked for.

Per-1M tokens (high-level, USD) — assumptions: 600 tokens request, 12 tokens generated avg, counts include both prompt + completion tokens:
- Redwood (hosted, on-demand): $9.50 / 1M tokens (no reserved commit)
- Redwood (Dedicated, amortized for pilot @ 6mo commit & expected utilization 65%): ~$4.90 / 1M tokens effective
- Anthropic (your current baseline, public estimate): ~$18–22 / 1M tokens depending on model variant
- AWS Bedrock (open model endpoints, estimate): ~$24–30 / 1M tokens depending on model and infra

Notes on assumptions and sensitivity:
- Cache: effective cost scales roughly linearly with cache hit — at 10% hit the effective cost is about 0.9x baseline; at 25% hit ~0.72x; at 40% hit ~0.60x. I put the full sensitivity table in the TCO sheet (tab: cache_sensitivity).
- Batching uplift: for your profile (bursty with regular micro-batches) we see 1.5–1.9x token throughput improvement depending on batch-window and concurrency. I included two scenarios: conservative (1.5x) and optimistic (1.9x).
- Burst behavior: continuous batching keeps p95 stable for steady traffic; for 1s spikes to 1.5k RPS we recommend a small buffer/burst pool — that keeps p95 within your 120ms SLO for the single-request path in our tests. More details in the benchmark PDF.

Proposed concrete tests on Tue Aug 17 10–12 PDT (your window confirmed):
1) Redwood runs synthetic harness against our hosted endpoint with your prompt set — collects: p50/p95 latency, throughput, cw-utilization, effective tokens consumed, cache hit rate.
2) FinPay runs same harness against Anthropic/Bedrock baseline and shares logs.
3) We do a side-by-side summary and a short 30-min sync Thu Aug 19 to review results and decide if we move to a Dedicated pilot.

I’m attaching the updated redwood-tco-modeling.xlsx that explicitly calls out sensitivity bands and a short benchmark checklist.

Marcus — can you confirm what security artifacts we’ll share for procurement (SOC2, pen-test summary, options for VPC/SAML)?

Thanks — I’ll send invites for the harness run and the follow-up review once Marcus confirms artifacts.

Aditya
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha / team —

Short answers from Ops/Security side: we can provide the following for the pilot/procurement review: 
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and summary of scope.
- Penetration test executive summary (recent).
- Network options: Dedicated includes a VPC peering option + customer-managed egress; for Private we have on-prem & air-gapped packaging available if required.

On Dedicated cost: the amortized numbers Aditya shared are conservative for a 6-month pilot with 65% utilization — if you expect higher burst isolation needs we can give a 1-month burst pool add-on (small incremental monthly fee) to guarantee headroom for 1.5k RPS spikes.

I’ll attach the SOC2 cover page and pen-test summary after internal approvals (should be by Monday).
